analysis:
The only change in this PR is one documentation row in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1751). It adds DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP to the table of environment variables read by the provider. The row says `0` disables the load-time shape warmup and `always` skips its shader-cache probe, with the source cited as ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (`shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey`). It sits in the table whose preceding text says only the listed variables are forwarded into the LaunchAgent plist's EnvironmentVariables (via passthroughEnvKeys + inferencePassthroughEnvKeys). Every other variable reaches the engine only under --foreground or --local. I could not check from the supplied evidence whether the new variable is actually forwarded to the daemon or only read in foreground mode. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not a vulnerability. Because the table sits under that passthrough sentence, the placement may misdescribe forwarding.

This is documentation only. No code, authorization, attestation, encryption or key handling changes, so no threat-model assets or boundaries are altered. T-041 and the prefix-cache TTL, HMAC and scoping controls are untouched. A warmup toggle is a local, operator-controlled performance setting. A warmup that runs on load could in principle change TTFT behavior, which is relevant to the TTFT oracle in T-041. The supplied evidence does not show the warmup using consumer data or cache entries, so I report no finding. The implementing code (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift) was not supplied. The next pass should check that warmup uses synthetic inputs, writes no persistent artifacts, and does not touch the SSD prefix cache or KEK. Units 4, 5 and 6 are base text with no relevant changes beyond the single added line.
